summary: Executed backend + frontend validation for Advance Mode protections, conditional Crypto Type Pass flow, Hardcore deletion behavior, and requested Settings/UI regressions on the live preview URL.

critical.issue: Credentialed CORS policy is still wildcard-based (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) and does not return `access-control-allow-credentials: true` in preflight response for tested origin.

action_items: Set explicit allowed origins in backend CORS config and return credential headers for allowed origins; avoid wildcard with credentialed auth policy.
Re-run backend preflight test after CORS config update and confirm browser cookie-based auth compatibility policies.
critical_code_review_comments: `backend/server.py` CORS branch for wildcard origins (`'*'`) conflicts with credentialed auth expectations and is the root cause of the failing preflight check.
Advance Mode backend protections are correctly enforced for reveal/update/delete/TOTP/share/bulk-delete in current implementation.
Seed admin logic now includes updating password hash when ADMIN_PASS changes (startup path looks correct in code review).
seed_data_creation: Created multiple TEST_it12_* users/items via backend API and UI flows.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated on preview URL: conditional birthday->complete when L3 disabled, birthday->layer3 quiz when enabled, one-time L3 view + export bypass, Advance Mode passphrase prompt for reveal/copy/edit/delete/TOTP in UI, non-Advance actions remain prompt-free, settings has no l3-view-btn and keeps l3-export-btn, mobile settings access works. Only remaining backend failure is credentialed CORS preflight policy.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: OPTIONS /api/auth/login with Origin + Access-Control-Request-* headers returns 204 with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and no `access-control-allow-credentials`. This fails credentialed CORS policy checks. Likely cause is wildcard CORS mode active in runtime env (`CORS_ORIGINS` effectively wildcard), which bypasses explicit-origin credential response behavior. Mitigation: configure explicit origins list (preview/prod URLs) and ensure middleware returns both `access-control-allow-origin` (specific origin) and `access-control-allow-credentials: true`.
